newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: OLYMPICS-BUENOS AIRES HOPES TO BE FIFTH-TIME LUCKY.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-BUENOS AIRES HOPES TO BE FIFTH-TIME LUCKY.

text.p: Local officials will be
praying for a change of fortune when the committee in charge of
selecting the venue for the 2004 Summer Olympics arrives in
Argentina on Monday.
After four failed attempts to host the Games, Buenos Aires
is braced for the 558 questions of the 20-member IOC committee,
led by Germany's Thomas Bach.
A factor which could give Argentina's capital an edge over
its rivals is the high density of sports facilities already
existing within a small area, local organisers say.
Twenty-four of the 28 Olympic competitions could take place
in a "loop" 14 km long and two km wide along the River Plate
coast.
Tourism Secretary Francisco Mayorga is confident Buenos
Aires will be shortlisted with three other cities when the
Olympic committee votes on March 7.
The host city will be named on September 7.
Buenos Aires has previously failed in its bids to hold the
Games in 1936, 1944, 1956, when it was runner-up, and 1968.
Hosting the Olympics would require $551 million of
investment, of which $284 million would be raised by the Olympic
Organising Committee and $267 million by the private sector
through television rights, contracts with sponsors, the sale of
stamps, souvenirs and tickets and other sources of income,
Mayorga said.
He estimated total profits would be $51 million.
The Games would also create 70,000 temporary jobs -- good
news for a country with 17 percent unemployment.
The proposed Olympic loop would stretch between the stadiums
of traditional soccer rivals Boca Juniors and River Plate, with
the Olympic Village next to Boca's ground, at the southern end
of the loop.
Heading north, the boxing venue would be the Luna Park
indoor stadium and volleyball would be played in the Punta
Carrasco and Costa Salguero facilities on the shores of the
River Plate.
The up-market district of Palermo would host weightlifting,
tennis would be played at the Buenos Aires Lawn Tennis Club,
hockey and softball at the Gimnasia y Esgrima club, shooting at
the Tiro Federal and the pentathlon at the CENARD sports
complex.
River Plate would become the Olympic stadium and the site of
athletics, swimming, diving and water polo.
Outside the loop, women's basketball would be held at the
Velez Sarsfield stadium, rowing in the nearby Tigre delta and
baseball in Ezeiza, close to the international airport.
Olympic soccer matches would be spread around the country at
the 1978 World Cup stadiums of Mar del Plata, Cordoba, Mendoza
and Rosario.
